answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a publicly verifiable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fraud. Reputation and voting weight accrue only to bonded identities, so creating a thousand sybils does not multiply influence unless the attacker also funds a thousand bonds. A cedar-themed agent, a glacier monitor, and a sable trader can all join, but the attacker pays real capital per identity and risks losing it if caught.
